full_judgment:
Ahsanuddin Chowdhury, J —This is a Reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the Special Tribunal, 2nd Court, Dacca (Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dacca) for confirm on of the sentence of death passed on 5.10.72 on the condemned prisoners Mokbul Hussain Ayub Ali and Zubair alias S. S Ahmed Ullah Two appeals, one by condemned prisoners Mokbul Hussain and Ayub Ali and another by Zubair have been filed against their conviction under section 302/109 of the Bangladesh Penal Code and Article 2(B) yead with Part IV (b) of Bangladesh Collaborators (Special Tribunals (Order, 1972 (President’s Order No. 8 of 1972) and the sentence of death under the former section. The two appeals have been numbered as Appeal No. 122 of 1972- Both the Reference and the appeals have been heard together and are being disposed of by this judgment.

2. The Prosecution case is that while Bangladesh was under the occupation forces of Pakistan and the enemy forces were about surrender and liberation of Bangladesh was imminent, the Pak army with the help of certain collaborators organised as Al Badars and Razakars engineered a scheme to annihilate the intellectuals of Bangladesh and in furtherance of that objective and also to sustain and maintain the occupation of the Pak Army the collaborates rendered active assistance to Pak Army to thwart the struggle for liberation daring the period of occupation commencing from 25th of March, 1971 when the Pak Army cracked down upon the people of Bangladesh. In furtherance of the said objective the condemned prisoners acted as collaborators being members of Al-Badars and in prosecuting the said objective five Al-Baders armed and clad with Khaki uniform entered the premises at 44, Shahaheb bari, Azimpur, known Daira Sharif at about 8-30 A. M. on the 15th of December, 1971. The Al Badrs has caps. Four of them covered their faces with handkerchiefs and one covered his face with a muffler and had also sunglass on his eyes. One of the glasses had a crack. On interrogation by those five Al-Badars the prioner Zubair pointed out the house of the victim Dr A.K.M Azad. They thereafter knocked at his door and the door having been opened by Dr. Azad himself, he was interrogated as to whether he was Dr. Azad Dr. Azad replied in the affirmative then the five Al-Badars searched the rooms for a few minutes and then forcibly took away Dr. Azad with intent to murder him or knowing that he would be murdered. Dr Azad's brother PW 1 Habibul Bashar who lived in a separate house to the north heard about the kidnapping of his brother from PW 3 Zakir Hossain and rushed to the house of Dr Azad from his own house, and when he was about to enter the house, the presoner Zubair told him that Dr. Azad had been taken away Al Badars to the residence of one Hajee Kashem, Chief of the Azimpur peace Committee and the guided him to that residence. A micro bus used by the Al-Badas at that time was still in front of the main gate of the house and Dr. Azad was kept inside the said micro bus. But being misguided by prisoner Zubair his efforts to find out and help his brother Dr. Azad were frustrated. On the same day at about  the same time those five Al-Badars kidnapped PW 12 Matur Raman and his brother Montu from the neighbouring house along with another named Bulu. PW 12 luckily escaped. Dr. Azad and Montu were done to death at Rayer Bazar from here the dead body of Dr. Azad was discovered and brought to the house of Dr. Azad where his mother Mrs Kohinoor Begum (PW 9), sisters Selina (PW10) Salma (PW 11) and two other brothers Ahul Khair and Zakir Hossain (PW 3) and another relative Abul Hossain Mallik (PW 18) were living with Dr. Azad on the date of occurrence. They as well as PW 1 Habibul Bashar and P W 2 Serajul Haq and another neighbour Dr. S. M. Anwar Hossain (PW 9) identified the dead body of Dr Azad which was later given burial in the New Azimpur Graveyard after offering the janaza prayer on the 18th of December, 1971.

3. It is further alleged that on the 31st December, 1971 at about 5 PM. condemned prsioners Mokbul Hossain and Ayub Ali were found on board a launch at Sadar-Ghat Dacca bound for Munshiganj. P.W 16 Kazi Mustafizur Rahman was going to Munshiganj by the same launch. Prisoner Mokbul was wearing sun-glass with a crack in one of the glasses. At the sight of these two prisoners P W 16 Mustafizur Rahman recognised them as two of the five Al-Badars who raided their house and kidnapped his two brothers Moutu and PW 12, Matiur Rahman. At that time P.W. 13 Abdul Halim came to that launch and PW 16 briefly narrated to PW 13 the occurrence in their house. As soon as PW 16 mentioned about the sunglass the prisoner Mokbul hastily removed the sunglass from his eyes and other prisoner realising the situation went round the cabin and signaled Mokbul to come out of the cabin. Both of them were however detained in the cabin and when the launch reached Katpatti Launch Ghat, Munshiganj they were handed over to the Muktibahini at the Ghat. They were detained at the Muktibahini Came till the 2nd of January, 1972. P.W. 12 Matiur Rahman was taken there and the recognised the prisoners to be two of the 5 Al-Badars who had raided their house. Thereafter they were produced to the Munshiganj police station where Mustafizur Rahman (PW 16) lodged a first Information Report regrding the occurrence in their house and a case was registered as Lalbagh P S. Case No. 19 (1) of 1972.

4. PW I Habibul Bashar lodged a First Information Report (hereinafter referred to as the FIR) on the 24th of January, 1972 naming Zubair as an accused along with 5 members of Al- Badars in respect of the murder of Dr. Azad who was kidnapped from his residence on 15-12-71 whereupon Lalbagh PS Case No. 125 dated 24th January, 1972 was stared. PW 26 A K.M. Shamsuddin, Inspector of police attached to Bangladesh CID took up the investigation of the case. In course of the investigation PW. 26 made a prayer to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, dacca  to show the prisoner Mokbul Hossain and Ayub Ali arrested in Lalbagh PS case No. 125 dated 24th January, 1972 (G R. Case N. 42/72). Accordingly, they were shown arrested in this case. Having completed the investigation PW 26 submitted charge sheet against prisoners Mokbul and Ayub Ali on the 20th April, 1972 and not against Zubair. Then under order of his superior officer, PW 26 made further investigation and submitted a supplementary charge sheet on the 16th June. 1972 against prisoner Zubair alias S S. Ahmedullah, who surrendered in court on 11-9-72 and thereafter the trial commenced.

5. The accusation against prisoners Mokbul and Ayub Ali was that they committed the offence under section 302/109 of the Bangladesh Penal Code as mentioned in Part I of the Schedule to the Bangladesh Collaborators (Special Tribunal) Order 1972 and were liable to be punished under article 11 (a) of the said Order, as on 15 12-71 at about 8-30 A.M they along with some other Al-Badars forcibly kidnapped Dr. Azad, a distinguished scholar and a supporter of the liberation struggle of Bangladesh, from his rented house at 44,  Azimpur Road, PS  Lalbagh, Dacca with intent to murder him or knowing that he would be murdered and that he was actually murdered.

6. Further accusation against them was that they committed the offence as described in clause (b) of the 4th part of the schedule to the Bangladesh Collaborators (Special Tribunals' Order, 1972 and liable to be punished under clause (d) of Article 11 of the said Order as they acted as collaborators of Pak army by giving them assistance and support for perpetuating and sustaining their illegal occupation of Bangladesh.

7. As against on prisoner Zubair, the accusation was that he on 15.12.71 at about 8-30 A.M. helped the Al-Badars, namely, prisoners Mokbul and Ayub Ali and some others in taking away by force Dr A.K.M. Azad from this residence which was shown by Zubair to the other two prisoner, who along with some other Al-Badars kidnapped Dr Azad with intent to murder him or knowing that he would be murdered and in fact he was murdered and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s 302/109 Penal Code.

8. Further accusation against Zubair was that he collaborated with the Pak army as a member of the Islamic chatra Sangha in thwarting the liberation struggle of the people of Bangladesh and sustaining the Pak army in their illegal occupation of Bangladesh under brute force,

9. The defence of prisoners Mokbul and Avub Ali was that they were quite innocent of the charges levelled against them, and that they had no knowledge of the alleged occurrence and they were not connected with any activity against the liberation movement. Their further case was that they were ordinarily day labourers and residents of PS Phulpur in the district of Mymensingh. After the liberation of Bangladesh they on the 30th of December, 1971 came to Dacca. from their respective village home to go to their respective father-in law's house in Munshiganj On the 31st of December, 1971 they started for Munshiganj to meet their respective wife and children and boarded a motor launch at Sadarghat at about 5 PM but unfortunately over the sitting accommodation in the said launch a quarrel cropped up between them and PW 16 Kazi Mustafizur Rahman and as result. PW 16 in collusion with PW 13 Abdul Halim falsely described them as Al Badars and Razakars and handed them over to some Mukti bahini in spite of their protest and subsequently implicated them in this case concocting a false story against them.

10. The defence of the other prisoner, namely Zubair was that in the morning of 15th December. 1971 five Albadars in uniform and shoes on and fully armed jumped into their premises, known as Dr. Sharif by one side of the Major Sharif and graveyard and to this he took exception and also raised a protest upon which the Al-Badars got annoyed and surrounded him pointing guns at him. threatened his life and then took him towards the northern site which was open. He saw outside 4/5 Al-Badars standing with position. Thereafter he was brought back by the north gate and was again threatened that they would put an end to his life if he did not tell them what they wanted. At that time they were in front of the house of Dr. Azad which is a one unit house within the premises of Zubair's ancestral house-Daira Sharif. They then questioned him about the owners of he houses to which he replied that the houses were theirs and on further questioning as to who lived in the house in front of which they were standing, he replied that their tenant Dr. Azad was living there. He gave that reply for fear of his life otherwise he would have been fired at. Having been let off. he went a little away and stood by the side of the mosque within the premises and having seen that Dr. Azad was being taken away he followed him along with the family members of Dr Azad upto the main gate to the south which was closed but was opened by their servant Taju out of fear under the orders of the Al-badars. His further defence was that he had some discord with the brothers of Azad and they took this opportunity to falsely implicate him although he was innocent of the occurrence and a supporter of the movement of Bangladesh and not connected with any organisation, against the said movement, that is to say, he was not a member of the Islamic Chatra Sangha. He was connected with Muktibahini.

11.The prosecution examined as many as 75 witnesses and 3 defence witnesses were examined by prisoner Mokbul Hossain. The learned Judge of the Tribunal having considered the evidence, found all the three prisoners guilty under both counts and sentenced them to death, as stated above.

12. Prisoners Mokbul Hossain and Ayub Ali have been represented in their appeal by Mr. Md. Abdur Rouf while the prisoner Zubair alias SS Ahmed Ullah has been represented In his appeal by Mr Abdul Hye Choudhury and Mr. A.T.M. Masud. Deputy Attorney General has appeared on behalf of the State.

13. Mr. Md. Rouf contends that the two prisoner represented by him have been falsely implicated in the case. They are completely innocent of the occurrence in respect of kidnapping of Dr. Azad The learned Judge of the Tribunal has entirely misconceived the case against them and committed a great error in law in convicting and sentencing them as aforesaid.

14. Mr. Abdul Hye Chowdhury has urged the following points in the appeal preferred by prisoner Zubair :-

1. The circumstance disclosed in the evidence are not incompatible with the innocence of Zubaur and the contrary view held by the Tribunal is wholly wrong,

2. The explanation given by Zubair for his conduct in reasonably true and he is, therefore, entitled to acquittal inasmuch as it is a case of no evidence.

15. It is to be noted that according to the prosecution case, PW 3 Zakir Hussain, a brother, Pw 9 Mrs. Kohinoor Begum, mother, PW 10 Selina, PW 11 salma, two sisters and PW 18 Abul Hossain Mallik, a cousin of Dr. Azad are the eye witnesses to the occurrence and of them PW 9 Mrs Kohinoor Begum appears to have first seen the 5 Al-badars in the premises of Shah Shaheb Bari. She deposed that on 15-12-71 at about 7-30 AM she woke up and finished a part of her usual work in the kitchen and while she was standing, at the window in the north of kitchen at about quarter to eight she saw Zubair going towards the north gate talking with five armed men with khaki uniform and Zubair opened that gate lock and they went outside the gate. Again 3/4 minutes after Zubair came back with those five Persons. Then seeing them coming she went to the dining room. While she was standing on the veranda of the dining room she heard Zubair telling them about the house of Dr. Azad and showing them the room he said that Dr. Azad was sleeping there. Then they got on the verandah and knocked at the door and she went to Azad's room through her room and saw her sons Zubair Hussain (PW 3). Abul Khayer and PW 18 Abul Hussain entering the room of Dr. Azad. Her laughers, PWs. Selina and Salma also came to that room. At the knocking of the door repeatedly her son Azad opened the door Then the men in uniform entered the room and asked if he was Dr. Azad. Dr Azad answered in the affirmative whereupon they asked Dr. Azad to remove the ladies for their search in the room. She heard them saying to Dr. Azad that he was to go with them. Hearing all this the witness went into the room of Dr Azad and asked him to dress up and not to go wearing lungi. Dr. Azad then dressed up and she asked them where they were taking her son. But she was pushed aside. Thereafter her daughter Salma embraced Dr. Azad obstructing his way and then they pushed aside her daughter too and took Dr Azad with them forcibly outside the room and they also followed up to the main gate on the south. The main gate was closed with inner passage open. 3 of the 5 Al Badars first crossed the gate and then her son crossed and thereafter the remaining two crossed. She could not proceed further as she was threatened. At that time Zubair was standing inside the premises and he asked one man, namely, their servant to lock up the gate and then all of them came back. A few minutes after PW 1 Habibul Bashar came and she narrated the occurrence to him. She further said that those 5 men were in Khaki uniform and four covered their faces with handkerchiefs and one had covered his face with a muffler and had glasses on his eyes.

16. PW 3 Zakir Hussain deposed that on 15.12.71 at about 8 or 8.15 he woke up from sleep and then went to the bathroom and when he came out from the bathroom he heard voices outside the room adjoining the outer verandah of their house and our of curiosity he opened the window and saw five persons who were armed and in uniform accompanied by zubair. Those five persons were in khaki uniform and cap with front as used by Razakars. One had a muffler tied round his face and was wearing sun-glasses, one glass of which was cracked and the other 4 had covered their faces he tying handkerchiefs below the nose. At that time he heard Zubair saying, pointing out the room of his brother Dr. Azad that it was the room of Dr. Azad and that he was sleeping there and then the witness entered the room. From inside he heard a heavy knocking and shouting in Bengali 'দরজা খোলো'  and then his brother Dr. Azad woke up from sleep and opened the door. When the door was opened those 5 persons entered the room and asked his brother if he was Dr. Azad and if was a Professor and on his answer in the affirmative they wanted to search the house and asked the females to go to on room and wait there. Then the Al-Badars searched the rooms and again came to the room of his brother Dr. Azad and asked him to go with them. Thereafter they pulled him away by the hand. One of them pushed aside his mother and did not hear her entreaties. His mother asked them to allow Dr. Azad to change his dress which they allowed and thereafter took him away. He then informed his brother PW 1 Habibul Basher about this occurrence. PW 10 Selina and PW 11 Salma, the two daughters of PW 9 gave practically the same version. The evidence of PW 18 is precisely the Same at that given by the other inmates of the house but he said nothing about Zabair. He however, claimed to have recognised AyubA Ali.

17. There is no dispute that Dr. Azad was kidnapped by five Al-Badars at about 8.30 A.M. on 15-12-71 from his residence within the premises 44, Daira Sharif  Azimpur and that on the 18th of December, 1971 his dead body was discovered from Rayer Bazar, The said body was identified to be dead body of Dr. Azad by P.W 1 Habibul Bashar, PW 2 Serajul noor Begum, PW 3 Zakir Hossain, PW 9 Mrs. Kohinoor Begom, PW 10 Selina, PW 11 Salma, PW l7 Golam Rasul Mallik, PW 18 Abul Hossain Mallik and also by PW 19 Dr. S.M. Anwar Hossain. All the witnesses who saw and identified the dead body deposed that they found bullet and bayonet charge injuries on the dead body of Dr Azad. From this evidence is can be safely held that Dr. Azad was murdered. The dead body was later given burial In the New Graveyard, Azimpur. PW 8 Md. Musa, a Muharrar at Azimpur Graveyard corroborated the fact of burial of the dead body of Dr. Azad, in New Graveyard, Azimpur on 18-12-71 and proved an entry in the Reserve Book, Azimpur new Graveyard at page 32 which was seized by the CID Inspector. The seizure list has been marked as Ext 4. The entry in the Reserve Book is serial No. 713.

<u>18. Now the question is whether prisoners Mokbul and Ayub Ali were two of the five Al-Badars who kidnapped Dr. Azad from his residence. The evidence which we has already noticed clearly shows that those five Al-Badars were in khaki uniform i.e. they had khaki pant, khaki shirt and also caps on their heads. Four of them covered their faces upto the nose with handkerchiefs and one covered his face with a muffler and had sun-glass. PW 16 while lodging FIR stated that some of the Al-Bodars had masks at the time of kidnapping his brother, Dr Azad. It, therefore, appears that those 5 Al-Badars took precaution to conceal their identity. Otherwise, they had no reason to cover their faces with handkerchiefs and muffler. It is to be mentioned here that prisoners. Ayeb Ali and Mokbul are men of police-station Peulpur is the district of Mymensingh. They were not known to the inmates of the residence of Dr. Azad either by name or by face. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has relied on the evidence of PW 3 Zakir Hussain and PW 18 Abut Hossain as regards the identification of Ayub Ali as one of the Al Badhar who had kidnapped Dr. Azad. In examination in chief PW 3 Zakir Hussain said that 5 persons were in khaki uniform and had cap with front as used by he Razakars in those days and one had a muffler tied round the face and was wearing sunglasses and mouth open. One glass of the sunglasses was cracked and the other four had covered their faces by tying handkerchiefs below the nose. Those persons were speaking in Bengali and at the time of speaking they were removing the handkerchiefs cover below the mouth. In cross-examination made on behalf of Ayub Ali the witness said that this accused (Ayub Ail) had an ash colour pullover. This he did not say in his examination-in-chief. .He did not also state to Investigation Officer that Ayub Ali downed his lace cover while taking. He has therefore, been contracted on this point by the investigation Officer who stated that Zakir Hussain did not state to him that while talking the face cover was downed by Ayub Ali. He (PW 3) of course, stated that he would be able to recognise the persons if shown again. Ayub Ali was placed at the Test identification Parade (T. I. Parade) but Zakir Hussain was not available, as a witness at T. I. Parade on 2 to 3 occasions. The prosecution had no explanation to offer as to why Zakir Hussain could not be made available as a witness to identify suspects at the T. I. Parade on 2 or 3 dates. It may also be pointed out here that PW 9 Mrs. Kohinoor Begum stated to the I.O that all the 5 Al-Badars had ash colour pullover on them. It is thus evident than the ash colour pullover on the person of any one of them had no special significance for the purpose of recognition and thereafter for identification of the accused on that basis.</u>

<u>19. The next witness so far as Ayub Ali is concerned is PW 18 Abul Hossain Mallik who identified Ayub Ali at the T. I. Parade which was held on 23-3-72. PW 8 Abul Hossain was examined by I.O. on 20-3-72 in the house of complainant PW I, only 3 days before the T.I. Parade. This T.I Parade was held by PW 15 Mr. M.I.H Chowdhury, Magistrate. His evidence shows that both Mokbul Hossain and Ayub Ali were placed at the T.I. Parade. PW 18 Abul Hossain Mallik identified Ayub Ali the person with arms amongst others. This T.I parade was held inside the court hajat. It is contended on behalf of Ayub Ali that the T.I. Prade was not held excluding the possibility of collusion and that he was shown before the T.I Parade was held we have already noticed that Ayub Ali and Mokbul Hossain were handed over to the Muktibahini at Katpatu Launch Ghat, Munshiganj, on 31.12.71 by PW 16 while they were going to Munshiganj by lunch in spite of their protest and then produced at Munshiganj Police Station on 2-1-72 where PW 16 lodged an FIR stating that those two prisoners along with 3 others raided their house on the same date and at about the same time when the house of Dr. Azad was raided and Dr. Azad was kidnapped. These two prisoners were shown arrested in the present case on 8-2-72 on the prayer of PW 26  I.O. while they were in custody in Munshiganj. From there Ayub Ali was brought to Dacca and produced in Court on 15-2-72. Again he was produced in Court on 1-3-72, and the T.I. Parade was held on 23-3-72. It is thus clear that at least on two occasions before the T. 1. Parade Ayub Ali was produced in court at Dacca where it was possible for anybody to see him. PW '8 is the General Manager, Eastern News Agency. The Eastern News Agency (ENA) distributed news about collaborators who were arrested and collected news and distributed such news relating to intellectual murder cases. He admitted while cross-examined on behalf of Ayub Ali, that he had curiosity to see those accused caught but he denied to have seen Ayub Ali except on the occasion when Dr. Azad was taken and on the date of T. I. Parade. Bat this witness said—</u>

<u>"I came to Court DSP and filed hazira at 10.30 or 11 and I was waiting there. I first went to Court Hajat and hearing that accused were not there then I went to Court Dy.S P. After 15/20 minutes or so 1 was taken to court hajat again and asked to go Inside and the escorting police remained outside the main gate. At the time when I received the last call as asked by a man to go there, then I found 20/24 prisoners. A man of such feature like this accused was only one there. Those prisoners were mainly wearing lungi, ganji, and some were bare bodied.</u>

<u>It is thus clear that sufficient precaution was not taken and mixing of the prisoners with other persons was not done in a manner to exclude the possibility of collusion. There was sufficient indication to enable witness to identify the prisoner. The learned Advocate appearing for Ayub Ali rightly contends that no value should be attached to this sort of identification inasmuch as the possibility of the accused being shown or seen was not altogether excluded. The learned Tribunal rejected this contention on the ground that if the witness had seen the prisoners before the T.I. Parade then he could have identified Mokbul as well. But the learned Judge seems to have lost sight of the fact that Mokbul was not brought to Dacca along with Ayub Ali from Munshiganj as it appears from the order sheet of the Magistrate's Court and as such there was no occasion to see Mokbul before the T.I. Parade with the result that PW 18 failed to identify him. So, it will not be safe to rely on the identification of Ayub Ali by FW 18. PW 18, however, claimed to have recognised this prisoner at the time of occurrence. It does not appear that he told anybody that he had recognised one of the Al-Badars. It was easy to depose in Court that he had recognised Ayub Ali. There being no corroboration on this point, we cannot accept this story of recognition of  Ayub Ali who was not known to him from before.</u>

<u>20. Let us now proceed to consider the evidence against Mokbul PW 3, 9, 10 and 11 are of the house of Dr. Azad. Mokbul was placed at the T.I. Parade but he was not identified by any of these witnesses at the T. I. Parade. He has, however, been connected with the occurrence on the basis of sunglasses. The prosecution case is that one of tie Al-Badars had put on sunglasses at the of occurrence. The prosecution wants to toy that the Al-Badrs with sunglasses was prisoner Mokbul even though none of the wit lasses could identify him. On the 31st December, 1971 prisoner Mokbul along with Ayub Ail was seen by PW 16 on board a launch at Sadarghat, Dacca and Mokbul had put on sunglasses. At once PW 16 took it to his head that one of the Al-Badars who had raided their house had sunglasses and this Mokbul must be that Al-Badar. Their further case is that the same Al Radar group kidnapped Dr. Azad from his credence. PW 16 further said that one of the sunglasses had a crack and similar crack was also found in one of the sunglasses of PW 12 when taken to Mukthibahini camp, Munshiganj where Mokbul was detained to see if he could identify any of the two prisoners Mokbul and Ayub Ali as the persons who along with some other had kidnapped him and his brother Montu identified Mokbul as one of the Al-Badrs particularly on the basis of sunglasses. He also came to have identified Mokbul at the T.I. Parade. The learned Trial Judge also has observed that Mokbul was identified by PW 12 at the T. I. Parade But PW 15, the Magistrate who held the T I. Parade did not say so. It is, therefore, difficult to follow how the learned Tribunal could accept that PW 12 identified Mokbul at the T. I. Parade. Moreover, having seen the prisoner Mokbul at Munshiganj and claiming him to be the person having used the sunglasses at the time of the occurrence in their house, the identification of Mokbul by PW 12 at the T.I. parade, if at all, has no value.</u>

<u>21. It is not disputed that prisoner Mokbul had sunglasses and that one of the glasses had a crack when they were seen by PW 16 on board the launch. Now the question is whether, because of his possession of such a sunglass he can be connected with the occurrence in the house of Dr. Azad. The evidence is that such sunglasses are available in the open market and any one can have such sun-glass and crack may also occur to such glasses. In cross-examination on behalf of Mokbul PW 16 says "I admit—To err is human. Goggles Ext. IV is a type of glass and may be had from market and such cracks in glasses may occur in some other glasses and may be worn by others also." The evidence further shows that those who work for sharpening Dao, knife etc. wear sunglasses. The evidence is that Mokbul works as a sharpener of knives, Dao etc. So, it was not unlikely that Mokbul would use sunglass. Here is great discrepancy   in the evidence whether the man having the sunglass at the time of occurrence was of dark or of fair complexion. PW 12 identified Mokbul from his dark compaction as an Al-Badar who put on black goggles. It is to he noted here that glasses have been variously recorded by the learned judge. He has described them as goggles and also as sunglasses. PW 16 said that during his talks with PW 13 Abdul Halim, the black ma went out of the cabin and turning to the window of the cabin was signalling the man with glasses to come out and that the fair looking man Mokbul was wearing the glass. There is, therefore sufficient room for doubt whether any one. Of these two prisoners was in the party of Al-Badars. PW 16 further deposed that as soon as he uttered the word "Chashma" at the time of his talks with PW 18 in the launch, Mokbul at once took off his and put it in the pocket and mat nervous, But PW 16 himself said that a man may have to open his sunglass at times to talk or see a thing clearly and PW 13 said that at that period (31st December, 1971) if any one was pointed out even wrongly as, then he would be unnerved and if people had started assaulting on such plea it could he difficult to stop it and it was natural for an outsider to become hesitant and nervous if such charge was level against him suddenly on the way. So, the fact that Mokbul put his sunglass is no indication of his guilty mind, because one may have to take off ores sunglass at times while talking and also to see a thing clearly. Furthermore, it was a time when the when the atmosphere was surcharged and it was quite easy to cow-down some one describing him either e as a Razakar or an al-Badar. PW 14 Anwar Hossain deposed that tie was a Mukthtibahini Commander and his camp was about one mile away from Katpatti Ghat where two armed Mukthtibahini used to stay. They along with PW 16 handed over Mokbul and Ayub Ali to him saying that they were involved in the occurrence in PW house. PW 6’s deposed that at the first sight he recognised Ayub Ali and Mokbul to be two of the 5 Al-Badars who raided their house. It is to be noted here that these two prisoners were not known to him from before. How could he recognize them at the first sight ? The only basis, it seems, was the sunglass of Mokbul which, in our opinion is no basis for recognition of unknown persons. These sunglasses are not uncommon and are available in market. We have examined the gasses, Ext. IV. We have found no special mark except the crack in one of them. It is not at all unusual that crack may occur in any one's glass. The prisoners contended that they had quarrel with PW 16 over sitting accommodation in the cabin and then in collusion with PW 13 they were handed over as Al Badars and Razakars at the Mukthibahini Camp in spite of protest. This contention cannot, in our opinion, be brushed aside having regard to tine circumstances then prevailing.</u>

<u>22. Now it is to be seen if the same gang of Al-Badars raided the house of Dr. Azad and that of PW 16. PW 16 said that all the 5 Al-Badars who raided their house had khaki uniform, grey caps and grey pullovers. PW 3 Zakir Hussain, a brother of Dr. Azad said that one of the At-Badars had ash colour pullover. He did not say if the tour others had any pullover or not. It appears that 5 Al-Badars who raided the house of PW 16 had khaki uniform and grey caps and grey pullover. But there is no evidence that the Al Badars who raided the house of Dr Azad had grey colour caps and grey pullovers. Further the evidence is that there was one group of 4 to 5 persons beyond the north gate of the preminses of Daira Sharif. PW 16 in his cross examination on behalf of Zubair said that besides the 5 Al-Badars here we others where the micro bus was kept. It is thus evident that there is the marked discrepancy in the evidence of the witnesses regarding the dress of Al Badars who raided the house of Dr. Azad and that of PW 16 Kazi Mustafizur Rahman and there is also evidence that there were more than one group of Al-Badars. The evidence adduced also shows that the two houses were raided at the same time. The same group of Al-Badars could not raid two houses situated at a distance of 150 to 200 yards at the same time. From this it is difficult to say that the same group of Al-Badars raided the house of Dr. Azad and that of Mustafizur Rahman. It is also to be noted that prisoners Ayub Ali and Mokbul were handed over to the Mukthibhini Camp on 31st December, 1971 at Munshiganj by PW 16 and thereafter were produced at Munshiganj police station where PW 16 lodged one FIR. The said FIR was not produced in the present case. The FIR in the present case was lodged by PW 1 on the 24th of January, 1972. After the handing over the two prisoners at the Mukthibhini Camp on 31st December, 1971, PW 16 had talks with PW 1 Habibul Bashar but the names of the two prisoners Ayub Ali and Mokbul were not mentioned in the FIR lodged by PW 1 on the 24th of January, 1972.  It was only stated in the FIR that PW 10 Selina sister of PW 1 described one of the Al-Badars as strong bult, short hair black complexion and flat nose PW. Selina in her deposition is completely silent about a man of this description. None of the other witnesses deposed that any of the 5 Al-Badars was of the feature and statute as finds mention in the FIR of PW 1. In the FIR there is no mention that one of the Al-Badars had sunglasses. It may be recalled here that it is on 8-2-72 that PW 26 A.K.M. Shamsuddin. Inspector of Police (CID) made a prayer to the SDO (Dacca) to show prisoners Mokbul and Ayub Ali arrested in connection with this case. This is how these two prisoners were implicated and brought on trial for abetment of murder of Dr. Azad. The learned Advocate representing these two prisoners has seriously contended that the prosecution implicated these two personnel in the occurrence relating to Dr. Azad on the evidence of witnesses of two occurrences, one to the house of Dr. Azad and another in the house of PWs 12 and 16 by concocting a story of sunglasses in respect of the one of them and a story of recognition regarding the other. But the attempt of the prosecution to implicate these two prisoners for abetment of the murder of Dr. Azad has been totally dashed to the ground. Considering the evidence as well as the facts and circumstances under which these two prisoners have been implicated in the case. We are of the view that the complicity not only of Ayub Ali but also of Mokbul as two Al-Badars having taken part in the occurrence in the house of Dr. Azad has not been established beyond reasonable doubt inasmuch as their identity as two of the 5 Al-Badars kidnapping Dr. Azad has not been established at all in this view of the matter we think that the conviction of the two prisoners u/s 302/09 B.P.C. cannot be sustained and the sentence of death passed there under against them cannot be affirmed.</u>

23. Now we proceed to consider the accusation against condemned prisoner Zubair, in this connection we are to refer to the relevant portion of the evidence of P.Ws. 3-9, 10 and 11 P.W. 3 Zakir Hussain deposed that he saw Zubair talking with 5 persons who were armed and in uniform and heard Zubair saying pointing out the room of his brother Dr. Azad that he saw sleeping there in cross-examination it was suggested that he did not state to I.O. that he saw Zubair talking with 5 persons and showing the room where Dr. Azad was sleeping. He denied the suggestion but PW 26 the I.O. deposed that PW 3 Zakir Hussain did not state to him that Zubair was talking to five Al-Badars and showing the house saying that Dr. Azad was sleep in the room. It is thus evident that PW 3 Zakir Hussain has been contradicted by the I.O. in respect of what he stated to court. PW 9 Mrs. Kohinoor Begum deposed as follows: “I saw our landlord’s son Zubair going towards north gate talking with five armed men in khaki uniform and Zubair opened the gate lock and they went outside the gate. Again 3/4 minutes after Zubair came back with those five persons. Then seeing them coming I went to the dining room opening the door. Then while I was standing on the verandah of the dining room I heard Zubair saying that this was the house of Dr. Azad and showing the room said that he was sleeping there.” Mrs. Kohinoor Begum further deposed that the main gate was closed with inner passage gate open. Three of the Al-Badars first crossed gate and then her son crossed and thereafter the remaining two crossed. She was trying to go out but was threatened. Zubair was standing by the side of the mosque inside Shah Saheb Bari and he asked one man to lock up the gate. Then as the gate was locked up she came back to the house. In cross-examination it was suggested to her that she did not state to I.O. all that she has stated to the I.O. what she stated in court. The evidence of PW 26 the I.O. shows that PW 9 did not state to him that Zubair opened the lock in north gate that Zubair told Al-Badars that Dr. Azad was sleeping in that room. She rather stated that she saw 5 Al-Badars wearing khaki pant and ash colour pullover and having pistol and rifles and hand marching off with Zubair in middle 3 men behind him and two men in front by the side of their house proceeding towards north gate and had gone outside the house. She also stated to I.O. that Tazu the servant of Shah Saheb Bari opened the gate and then Al-Badars went out with Azad scolding and prohibiting them from going further and that Zubair also accompanied them (inmates of the house) and stood near the mosque. PW 9 Mrs. Kohinoor Begum has been contradicted what she stated to the I.O. PW 10 Selina deposed that she saw 5 men with arms went towards north with Zubair and they were talking and then Zubair opened the door lock and went out and again came back and stood before the gate in front of their verandah Zubair showed the house of Dr. Azad and also the room saying that Dr. Azad was sleeping there. In cross-examination she was challenged that she did not state anything about Zubair to the I.O. She denied the suggestion but the I.O. stated that Selina did not mention the name of Zubair in any point of her statement. She did not state about any part of action by Zubair there. She stated those two men with arms and two other armed men stood on guard in front and rear of their house. Selina has been contradicted by the I.O. in respect of what she deposed in court. PW 11 Salma deposed that Zubair was with 5 armed men and he identified the house and told them that in that room. Dr. Azad was sleeping. She further said that she saw Zubair standing near the mosque, while the armed men took away her brother. In cross-examination she said that she heard Zubair saying that it was the house of Dr. Azad and he showed the room where Dr. Azad was sleeping. Those men were not talking to Zubair P.W. 11 Salma stated to the I.O. that Selina told that Al-Badars were taking away Zubair. It may be mentioned here that PW 18 was in the house at the time of occurrence but he is silent about Zubair. This witness is brother of PW 17 Gulam Rasul who is Bhagnipati of PWs. 3, 10 and 11. It appears from the evidence of PWs. 3, 9, 10 and 11 that Zubair showed the house as well as the room in which Dr. Azad was sleeping but they suppressed the circumstances under which he had to do so. It has transpired that Zubair having fallen completely in the gap of Al-Badars had to show the house and the room under threats of instant death.

<u>24. Further case of the prosecution is that if Zubair did not show the house of Dr. Azad to the 5 Al-Badars, Dr Azad could not be kidnapped and that he also misled P.W.1 Habibul Bashar telling him that Al-Badars had taken his brother to the residence of Hajee Kashem. But he was not taken there. Thereby Zubair frustrated the efforts of Habibul Bashar to help rescue his brother from the custody of Al-Badars who were still then in the micro bus on the rea to the south of the south gate and Zubair intentionally did so because he belonged to the Al-Badars being a student of Alia Madrasa and a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha. The defence seriously disputes these charges against Zubair. It is first to be seen if Zubair belonged to the Al-Badars and was a member of “Islamic Chatra Sangha”. In corroboration of the charge that Zubair was a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha which was affiliated to reactionary political parties, namely Jamaat-e-Islami, Muslim League e.t.c. who were against the Bangladesh movement. The prosecution examined PW 23 Sikandar Mia who was a man of Laksham in the district of Comilla. His evidence is that he was a rickshaw puller. But he gave up that profession and started selling ‘Pan’ from August, 1971. He used to sell ‘Pan’ and cigarettes in front of the medical college hostel at Bakshibazar in September/October 1971. There was a conference in Alia Madrasha where he saw Zubair with a rifle in hand and in Khaki uniform and a cap on his head. He saw him at Alia Madrasha gate. The witness further deposed that he worked as a domestic servant in the house of Zubair’s uncle near the house of Zubair in Daira Sharif. In cross-examination the witness failed to state the date and the period of the conference at Alia Madrasha. He could not also say the purpose of the conference. It may be noted here that Zubair was not sent up in the charge sheet which was submitted on 20th April 1972 against the other two prisoners. But under direction of the superior officer the IO PW26 filed a supplementary charge sheet against Zubair on 16th of June 1972. PW 23 Sekandar Mia was examined by the IO on 30th July after submission of the supplementary charge sheet. It is difficult to follow why such an important witness for the prosecution could not be found out by the IO before the submission of the supplementary charge sheet. It is strange that after submission of the charge sheet and the supplementary charge sheet, evidence was still being collected. This certainly goes to show that unusual procedure was adopted by the prosecution in the case. The evidence of the IO shows that Mr. Jalaluddin was the Principal of Alia Madrasha. He was residing in the quarters within Alia Madrasha. He was examined by the IO and was also charge sheet witness. He was a competent person to say if there was any conference of Islami Chatra Sangha in September/October in Alia Madrasha and whether Zubair was a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha. It is not denied that Zubair was a student of Alia Madrasha. That does not necessarily mean that he was a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha. The best evidence was withheld by the prosecution. The presumption must go against the prosecution u/s 114 illustration (g) of the Evidence Act. Another piece of evidence to show that Zubiar was an Al-Badar are two photographs (exts 1 and 2). Ext 1 is a group photograph and ext 2 is a passport size photograph. PW 1 himself expressed his inability to connect Zubair with the passport size photograph. The group photograph (ext 1) contains the photos of some persons including that of Zubair. The photo of one Nurul Haq is said to be an Al-Badar and a case against him is said to be pending. Simply because the photo of Nurul Haq said to be an Al-Badar is there with that of Zubair the process through which this photograph was collected sets one to thinking. The police seized the photograph from the office of PW 1 Habibul Bashar. With this photograph PW25 Raisuddin Bhuiyan went to PW 24 Fazlul Karim a News Editor, Dainik Bangla a few days after the liberation for publication stating that this was the photograph of Al-Badars. PW24 advised PW25 Raisuddin Bhuyan first to lodge a general Diary at the Thana. Accordingly PW 24 lodged a General Diary, Ext 8 at the Thana and thereafter it was published in the Dainik Bangla PW 24 in cross examination on behalf of Zubair said that at the time many people had given such photographs but they did not publish all. He could not; however, recollect as to who produced which photographs and when there is no evidence on the side of the prosecution in which year and at what time the group photograph was taken. The prisoner himself has stated while examined u/s 342 Cr. P.C that in 1969 AD he had gone to Sylhet along with some other students and a Lecturer. This group photograph was taken there. There is nothing to controvert this statement of Zubair. We, therefore, accept this statement that this group photograph was taken in the year 1969 A.D. when the formation of Al-Badars Razakars, etc., was not in the imagination of any person.</u>

25. In this connection the defence contends that P.W. 1 Habibul Bashar has falsely implicated the prisoner Zubair because of same discords between him and the prisoner P.W. 1 is an Editor of “Daily Evening Post”. He went to Karachi in May 1971 to attend the Editors Conference, Zubair requested him not go to Karachi at that time Further when P.W. Selina, sister of P.W. 1 appeared at the S.S.C. Examination in 1971, Zubair objected to her appearing at that Examination as it was against the directive of the Government of Bangladesh Moreover the son of Mr. Wahiduzzaman who was a Muslim Leaguer was a business partner of P.W. 1 whereas prisoner Zubair was pro-Bangladesh, P.W. 1 was therefore bearing grudge against him. Further it has been shown by the defence that, a magazine under the caption “Bishforan” was published in 1970 by the boys of the locality of Dhira Sharif and in that magazine Zubair wrote an article titled “Amar Ekusha” which has been marked Ext. A P.W. 9 Dr. S.M. Anwor Hossain has testified to this fact P.W. 19 has also deposed that Zubair was an anti-Pakistan and pro-Bangladesh. In view of all these facts we feel no hesitation to find that Zubair was not an al Badar not a member of the Islamic Chhatra Sangha not a Razakar.

26. Now, he us see whether Zubair’s showing the house and the room of Dr. Azad amounted to abetment of commit murder of Dr. Azad. None of the witnesses examined in the case by the prosecution could say how the Al-Badars first entered into the premises of Azimpur Shah Shaheb Bari. The evidence shows that the entire premises is surrounded by a wall. There are two gates the main gate is on the south by the main road and a smaller gate is on the north. In the main gate there is an inner passage gate. There is a small path way from the main gate towards north. To the east of small pathway stands a building which was in occuration of Shah Sabeb Bari. The evidence further shows (vide cross-examination of P.W. 16) that if the main gate to the south is closed then no one can enter the premises except by scaling the wall on the side of the gravey and by the south West, Zubair in his statement u/s, 342 Cr.P.C. stated as follows:-

“ I am not connected with the death of kidnapping of Dr. Azad nor did i render any abetment in the matter. I was not a member of the Islamin Chhatra Sangha and the evidence that has been adduced (in this regard) is false. I was connected with the Mukhtibahini and I rendered assistance to them. I showed the certificate granted by the Muktibahini in this respect to Inspector. There was curfew imposed on 15-12-71. The main gate was closed. At that time five persons entered into the Mazar Sharif with arms and shoes by crossing over the south-western wall and I raised protest saying “you are dishonoring the Mazar Sharif and you are trespassing into others house”. At that they became annoyed and surrounded me pointing guns at me and took me to the northern side of our gate. The gate was already lying open Going there I saw 5/6 persons standing with position. When (they) told them about me I was threatened with murder, And in that state, i.e. two persons in my front and three persons behind me I was taken there and they brought me there stating that if I did not speak the truth they would put an end to my life and they brought me to the northern side of the hauz (water reservoir) meant for ablution on the south-western corner of the house of her. Azad and caused me to stand there and put questions to me one after another and asked who is the owner if this house? I replied ‘It is ours’ Then they asked, who resides here? I replied ‘A tenant resides, when they asked as to who is the person residing I replied Dr Azad. I gave this reply for fear of may life otherwise they would have fired gunshot at me. After my replies when Dr. Azad was being taken away by then, Dr. Azad’s mother, brother and sister proceeded (up to the gate). The gate was lying closed. The members of the Al-Badar then asked our domestic servant Taju to open the gate whereupon he opened the gate out of fear. Thereafter they took away Azad Sb with them.”

27. The above statement of Zubair gets support from the statements of P.W. Salms to the IO. It is under the above circumstance on point of gun that Zubair had to show the house of Dr. Azad, P.W. 16 stated in cross-examination on behalf of Zubair that at that time they did not have the courage to act contrary to their command (Pak. Army or Al-Badar) as at that time they feared that they could kill then by firing. It has therefore been clearly brought out by the defence that Zubair completely feen into the grip of 5 Al-Badars who threatened him that he would be put to death if he did not tell them what they wanted from him whatever Zubair did was done on point of gun and not with any criminal intent nor with any knowledge that Dr Azad being kidnapped would be murdered.

28. It is now to be seen if Zubair frustrated the efforts of P.W. 1 to help rescue his brother Dr. Azad, by telling him that Dr. Azad might have been taken to the house of Hajee Kashem and leading him to that house, P.W. 1 deposed that as soon as he reached the north gate of the house having been informed that his brother had been kidnapped he found Zubair on the north gate and charged him where they had taken his brother and Zubair reluctantly told him that his brother might have been taken to the house of Hajee Kashem, Chairman, Azimpur Peace Committee and his house was adjoining to the premises No. 44, Azimpur. Then Zubair directed him to the house of Hajee Kashem through inside passaged and showed him the way to enter the house of Hajee Kashem by scalling a wall. Then he scaled the wall and went to the house of Kashem but Zubair did not scale the Wall P.W. 1 met Hajee Kashem who told him that his brother had not been taken there P.W. 1 could not trace out which way his brother was taken by the Al-Badars as a result of Zubair’s misguiding him to the house of Kashem. The defence denies this charge. Even assuming that Zubair said so and did so, he might have said and done so from his impression that if anybody could be of any help and assistance in a matter like this the Chairman of the peace Committee was the person as in those days the Chairman of the Peace Committee wielded sufficient influence. P.W. 1 himself from the house of Hajee Kashem contacted the Lalbagh P.S. over phone and asked for help but he was informed by the police that they were helpless in this matter. So, even if it be assumed that the microbus carrying Dr. Azad was still there at a distance of 40/50 yards from the south gate of the premises of Shah Shaheb Bari P.W. 1 could not be of any help to his brother Dr. Azad. In the house there were Zakir Hussain, Abul Khair and Abul Hussain who could not be of any help. Furthermore, the evidence is that on the same date and about the same time P.W. 12 Matiur Rahman and his brother Montu were kidnapped from their house and they were taken along with Dr. Azad by the same microbus, P.W. 16 Mustafizur Rahman full brother of P.W. 12 and Montu could not render any help to his brothers. The evidence rather shows that P.W. 16 could not even come out of the gate of their own house. So, it passes our comprehension as to how Zubair misled P.W.1 Habibul Bashar and frustrated his efforts for rescuing his brother Dr. Azad from the clutches of Al-Badars. There is no evidence whatsoever that Zubair had knowledge that the microbus was still standing there. Curfew had been clamped in the city of Dacca and nobody could come out of his house during the period of curfew. So, it is not possible even to infer knowledge of Zubair about the microbus being there when P.W. 1 came to the house.

29. Let us now consider the point of law urged in this case. The charge is of abetment of the offence of murder, Section 107 of the Penal Code defines abetment as follows:

“A person abets the doing of a thing who-

Firstly: Instigates any person to do that thing or

Secondly: Engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing if an act or illegal omission takes place in pursuance of that conspiracy and in order to the doing of that thing or

Thirdly: Intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.

Explanation 1: A person who by wilful misrepresentation or by wilful concealment of a material fact which he is bound to disclose voluntarily causes or procures or attempts to cause or procure a thing to be done is said to instigate the doing of that thing.

Explanation 2: Whoever either prior to or at the time of the commission of an act does anything in order to facilitate the commission of that act and thereby facilitates the Commission there is said to aid the doing of the act.”

<u>30. The learned Deputy Attorney General has argued that the third clause of section 107 of the Code is attracted in this case, as the prosecution case is that Zubair intentionally aided by his act the lifting of Dr. Azad from his house. He has also drawn our attention to Explanation 2 stating that the act of Zubair facilitated the lifting of Dr. Azad from his house. A person abets by aiding when by any act eitaer prior to or at the time of the commission of an act he intends to faeilitate the commission thereof. A mere giving of an aid without any intent rather under threat of life on point of gun will not make the act an abetment of an offence. We have already noticed the evidence adduced by the prosecution and also the circumstances under which the prisoner Zubair acted. We have no doubt in our mind on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the evidence that Zubair did not intentionally aid by his act the lifting of Dr. Azad. He had to do it under duress, coercion and threat of life. If a person does an act under such circumstances he cannot be said to have intentionally aided an act for the consequences of which he is to be held liable. In order to be an accomplice, a person must have mens rea. A person does not become an accomplice by assisting another person to commit an offence unless voluntarily and knowingly giving that assistance and knowing that the offence is being or likely to be committed, This is so even if the offence is one of strict it cannot be held that Zubair acted as an accomplice in, kidnapping Dr. Azad for being murdered. The mother of Dr Azad asked her son Dr. Azad to change his dress and not to go with lungi on. Dr. Azad accordingly changed his dress. It seems that they did not even know that the murder of Dr. Azad would be committed or it was contemplated. Mr. Abdul Hye Chowdhury learned Advocate has referred us to certain decision, namely, the decisions reported in (1)1047 (1) K.B. 997; (Rex Vs. Steans) (2) A.I.R. 1957 Allalhbad 184 (Bachchan Lal Vs. The State) and (3) I.L.R.52 Calcutta 112 (Umadasi Dasi Vs. Emperor).</u>

31. In the case reported in 1947 (1) K.B. 997 the appellant a British subject was charged with doing an act likely to assist the enemy with the intent to assist the enemy entering the services of the German broadcasting system contrary to Reg. 2A of the Defence (General Regulations 1939). The appellant did enter that service and broadcast through that system, but gave evidence that this was done under the pressure of threats and of beatings up and with a view to saving his wife and children (who were in Germany) from a concentration camp. The trial judge directed the jury that if they though that what the appellant did was to help the enemy then unless he was without any intention at all by reason some duress, he must be taken to have intended the natural consequence of his deliberate act. The appellant was convicted and on appeal it was contended for the Crown that the saving of his wife and children from a concentration camp might have been the appellant's motive for his act but this was irrelevant on the issue of whither he acted with the intent alleged. The proper direction to the jury here was that the prosecution must prove the intent to assist enemy and that while the jury would be entitled to presume that intent if they thought the broadcasting was done as the result of the free uncontrolled action of the accused, they would not be entitled to presume it if the circumstances showed that the act was done ii subjection to the power of the brutal enemy or was as consistent with an innocent as with a criminal intent. The conviction was quashed. It was held that where an act was done by a reason in subjection to the rower of others. viz, the power of a brutal enemy an inference could not be drawn that he intended the natural consequence of such an act merely from the fact that he did it. The euilty intent could not be presumed but must he proved.

<u>32. In the case reported in A.I.R, 1957 Allahabad 184 the accused appellant's deem was that he held the legs of the deceased under threat of instant death and helped the murderers in removing the body and concealing it. Considering the facts and circumstances it was held by the Allahabad High Court that ordinarily the accused is responsible for his own acts and is not responsible for the acts of others, unless the law specifically makes him responsible for the acts of others. Where in a case of murder it was sought to infer the necessary intention on the part of the accused from the fact than he held the legs of the deceased while the other killed him and there was nothing to show that those others committed the acts in furtherance of common intention between them and the accused but on the other hand the accused's act was committed under duress this was a case where intention of the accused could not be presumed from the natural consequences of his conduct and the conduct of the others who were acting simultaneously at the time. When he did not act voluntarily and acted under threat of instant death he could not be said to have had any of the intentions necessary to make him liable for the offence of murder and therefore his conduct in holding the legs of the deceased would not amount to the commission of the offence of murder. His own act also was not no imminently dangerous that it must in all probability have caused death. His conduct would not amount to the offence of murder. The decision in the case Rex Vs. Steans reported in 1947 (1) K.B. 997 has been followed in this case.</u>

<u>33. In the case reported in I.L.R. 52 Calcutta 112 the appellant was tried jointly with one Nabani Dhor Mondal for the murder of her husband. Both were charged u/s. 302 of the Penal Code and the appellant was further charged u/s 302/109 P.C. the appellant was acquitted of the charge of murder but was convicted u/s 302/109 P.C. and sentenced to transportation for life. The Jury were divided as 5 to 4 as regards the charge u/s 302 against the other accused, On reference to the High Court by the Sessions Judge, the said accused was acquitted by the High Court. In this case the appellant made a statement of the nature of a confession implicating herself and Nabani. This incriminating statement was subsequently retracted. In her statement she said that Nabani murdered her husband while she held his legs. She said that she protested but when she was threatened with death she only assisted Nabani by holding legs of her husband. The High Court held that learned Sessions Judge overlooked the provisions of section 94 of the Penal Code. It has been hell that under section 94 of the Pedal Code a plea of compulsion by threats which reasonably cause the apprehension of instant death is a good defence by a person charged with any offence except murder and offences against the State punishable with death. The word "murder" in section 94 P.C. cannot be held to include abetment of murder. The appellate was acquitted of the charge u/s 302/109 P.C. on the ground that she acted under the apprehension of instant death. This decision has been based on section 94 of the Penal Code which provides as follows:</u>

<u>"Except murder and offences against the State punishable with death nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is compelled to do it by threats which at the time of doing it reasonably cause the apprehension that instant death to that person will otherwise be the consequence provided the person doing the act did not of his own accord or from a reasonable apprehension of harm to himself short of instant death place himself in the situation by which he became subject to such constraint.</u>

<u>"Explanation 1 :—A person ho of his own accord or by reason of a threat of being beaten joins a gang of dacoits knowing their character, is not entitled to the benefit of this exception, on the ground of his having been compelled by his associates to do anything that is an offence by law.</u>

<u>"Explanation 2—A person seized by a gang of dacoits and forced by threat of instant death to do a thing which is an offence by law for example, a smith compelled to take his tools and to force the door of a house for the dacoits to enter and plunder it is entitled to the benefit of this exception".</u>

<u>The learned Deputy Attorney General did not place any authority against the above ones.</u>

<u>34. In view of the decisions referred to above and the explanation offered by the prisoner Zubair regarding the circumstances under which he bad to point out the house of Dr. Azad it is to be considered if the facts and circumstances are incompatible with the innocence of the prisoner Zubair. Zubair stated that he did not intentionally or voluntarily aid the Al-Badars and that he pointed out the house of Dr. Azad under threats of instant death on gun point. There is nothing to show that Zubair had any liaison or nexus with the Al-Badars who entered the premises by scaling the wall and took Zubair in their grip. Zubair did not identify Dr. Azad to Al-Badars for kidnapping Dr. Azad. We are of the view that the facts and circumstances disclosed in the evidence are not incompatible with the innocence of Zubair and that the contrary view held by the learned Tribunal is entirely wrong and the explanation given by Zubair for his conduct is reasonably true and even if the prosecution case is fully believed the guilt of Zubair as an abettor has not been established.</u>

<u>35. It is true that an illustrious son of Bangladesh who was a Ph. D. in Mathematics, a Gold Medalist and a Fellow of Institute of Applied Mathematics in England and attached to the Institute for Advancement of Science and Technology Teaching in Bangladesh was kidnapped by the Al-Badars from his residence and thereafter he was cruelly and brutally murdered and his dead body was recovered from Rayer Bazar and given burial in the new graveyard at Azimpur. Dr. Azad was a great intellectual and an asset of the country. The void created by his tragic death can hardly be filled up. The heart really bleeds on account of the tragic end of such a valuable life. But justice is blind. In the domain of justice feelings, emotions or sentiment have no part to play. Justice is to be done on carefully considering the facts and circumstances involved in the case and weighing the evidence on record. In the instant case the prosecution has miserably failed to establish the identity of prisoners Mokbul and Ayub Ali to be two out of 5 Al-Badars who had kidnapped Dr. Azad. It has also failed to prove that prisoner Zubair intentionally, actively and purposely abetted the Al-Badars in kidnapping Dr. Azad. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case together with the evidence on record we accept the points urged by the learned advocates for the prisoners and we find no reason to maintain the conviction under section 302/109 PC against the prisoners and confirm their sentence of death thereunder. Accordingly the reference made by the learned Judge of the Tribunal for confirmation of the sentence of death is liable to be rejected.</u>

36. We now take up for consideration the second charge of collaboration against all these three appellants. So far as appellant Mokbul Hossain is concerned there is no evidence of his collaboration with the Pak Army as contemplated under Article 2(b) of President’s Order No. 8 of 1972. Furthermore, appellant Mokbul examined three witnesses in support of his defence that he was not a collaborator at all. The witnesses are DW 1 Mohon Chandra Sarkar, DW 2 Mir Abdur Rob and DW 3 Md. Golam Hussain. DW 1 Mohon Chandra Sarkar is the Chairman, Shakuai Relief Committee. He says that he knows appellant Mokbul and his father too. He has granted a certificate to the effect that Mokbul Hossain is known to him and that he is a citizen of Bangladesh and is not an Al-Badar or Razakar. He gave the certificate, Ext B. In cross examination, of course, he has said that during the period of disturbance and occupation they shifted to Meghalaya in India. But this does not mean that he had no contact with his locality and did not know what was happening there. He asserted that Mokbul Hossain was not a Razakar. PW 4 Hafizuddin Bhuiyan in his cross examination on behalf of Mokbul has said that D.W. 1 Mohon Chandra Sarkar is a renowned man and a worker of Awami League, P.W. 5 and P.W. 6 have also said in their cross-examination by Mokbul that Mohon Chandra Sarkar, Chairman of Shakuai Relief Committee is a renowned man and a worker of Awami League. This shows that he is a prominent man of the locality and respected by all. He has deposed that Mokbul Hossain was neither a Razakar nor an Al-Badar. D.W. 2 Mir Abdur Rob is the Chairman of Shakuai Gram Committee. He says that he knows Mokbul and he also granted him a certificate. He has further said that upto 16th December, 1971 they were engaged in helping Mukibahini and the allied army who passed through their area to Mymensingh. He has denied the suggestion that he gave a false certificate at the request of Mokbul’s father. D.W. 3 Golam Hussain is the Secretary, Shakuai Union Awami League. He says that he knows appellant Mokbul and his family. He has further said that they were helping and co-operating with the Muktibahini and the allied forces for arranging food, ammunition and shells. After this clear evidence, it is difficult to hold that Mokbul was either a Razakar or an Al-Badar or that he collaborated with the Pak Army. He is, therefore, found not guilty of this charge as well and the order of conviction  passed against him under the second charge that is the charge of collaboration with the Pak Army is liable to be set aside.

37. So far as appellant Ayub Ali is concerned the prosecution has examined some witnesses namely P.W. 4 Hafizuddin Bhuiya, P.W. 5 Abdur Rahman, P.W. 6 Abdul Aziz Khan, P.W. 7 Abdul Huq and P.W. 20 Abdul Majid. From the evidence of P.W. 4, 5 and 6 it appears that Ayub Ali worked in his locality as a Razakar and he also once looted a family towards Haluaghat P.W. 7 who was the officer-in-charge, Phulpur P.S. got an enquiry slip from the C.I.D. Inspector Shamsuddin regarding enquiry of antecedent and character of Ayub Ali. On enquiry it was found that he was a Razakar, P.W. 20 Abdul Majid S.I. of Police attached to Phulpur P.S. has deposed that the name of Ayub Ali appears in payroll Ext. 7 as Razakar in the Phulpur P.S. for the period from 16th September, 1971 to 30th September, 1971 for Platoon No. 5 and serial No. 15 shows that the payment was made to Ayub Ali, son of Karam Ali of village Bashtali and it contains the L.T.I. of Ayub Ali taken by the witness while disbursing his pay, vide Exts. 7(1) and  7(2). It may be noted here that Ayub Ali comes from Phulpur P.S. in the district of Mymensingh. This evidence clearly proves that Ayub Ali was a Razakar Ayub Ali is a man of the district of Mymensingh and the case against him was started in the district of Dacca. A question may naturally arise as to whether he can be tried by a Court in the district of Dacca as it has not been proved that he did any overt act as a Razakar anywhere in the district of Dacca, Clause (3) to Article 9 of President’s Order No. 8 of 1972 provides that a person accused of an offence punishable under this order may be tried a Special Tribunal or a Special Magistrate as the case may be, anywhere in Bangladesh. This appellant was placed on trial before the Special Tribunal Dacca. In view of this Provision the trial held against him by the Special Tribunal, Dacca is not without jurisdiction. The learned Tribunal has found this appellant to be a collaborator for being a Razakar and convicted him accordingly but he has not awarded any sentence on that court. This Court is quite competent to pass an order of sentence having found this appellant to be a Razakar. The minimum sentence as provided under Article 11(d) of the Collaborators Order is three years. We accordingly sentence him to three years rigorous imprisonment.

38. As regards the second charge against appellant Zubair we have already found on discussing the materials both for and against him that he was not an Al-Badar nor a Razakar nor a member of Islamic Chhatra Sangha and as such he is not a collaborator within the meaning of Article 2(b) of President’s Order No. 8 of 1972. He was anti-Pakistani and pro Bangladesh. He is accordingly found not guilty of this charge as well.

39. In the result the Reference is rejected. The appeal preferred by appellants Mukbul Hossain and Zubair alias S.S. Ahmed Ullah is hereby allowed. The order of conviction under section 302/109 of the Bangladesh Penal Code and under Article 2(b) read with part IV(b) of the Bangladesh Collaborators (Special Tribunals) order, 1972 (President’s Order No. 8 of 1972) and the sentence of death passed against them under the former section is hereby set aside. They are found not guilty and acquitied of the charges levelled against them. It is directed that the said appellants Mukul Hossain and Zubair alias S.S. Ahmed Ullah be set at liberty forthwith, if not wanted in connection with any other matter. The appeal preferred by appellant Ayub Ali is allowed in part. The order of conviction and sentence of death passed against him u/s 302/109 B.P.C. is set aside and he is found not guilty and acquitted of the charge levelled against him on this country. But his conviction under Article 2(b) read with part IV (B) of the Bangladesh Collaborators (Special Tribunals) Order, 1972 is affirmed and he is sentenced to suffer 3 (three) years”, rigorous imprisonment thereunder.

Ruhul Islam, J.- I agree.

End.
